headline: Carry a separate path total to each leaf
statement: Return whether a binary tree contains a root-to-leaf path whose node values sum to targetSum. A leaf has no children; a path ending at an internal node does not count.
intuition: Every stack entry should contain both a node and the total along the unique root-to-that-node path. Siblings inherit the same parent total but accumulate independently. Only leaves can complete the requested path.
approach: Return false for an empty tree.
Start a DFS stack with root and its value.
At a leaf, compare its total with targetSum.
For each child, push the child with total plus the child’s value.
correctness: The initial total equals the root path’s sum. Pushing a child adds exactly its value, preserving the stack invariant for every entry. Every leaf is visited unless a matching one is found earlier, so true is returned exactly when a root-to-leaf path meets the target.
bruteForce: Enumerate all root-to-leaf node sequences, then sum each sequence separately; storing and summing paths adds repeated work.

complexity.explanation: Each node is processed once. DFS pending entries use O(h) space in a binary tree, and iteration avoids recursion limits.

pitfalls: A target reached at an internal node is not enough.
Negative values prevent simple pruning when a sum exceeds target.
An empty tree has no root-to-leaf path even when target is zero.
